diagnostic:
S2 resumed after the D10 revision. Readiness now follows the mount page: usePageFreshQuery records the mount page once in a useState initializer. A component is ready when the last good answer's askedOnPage is at least its mount page, and it keeps that answer through later asks and failures. It is failed when it has no such answer, nothing is in flight and the latest ask failed (the permissive fallback with loadFailed true). Otherwise it is loading. The current page is never compared and isFetching never drives loading. The queryFn returns PageFreshAnswer {answer, askedOnPage} and throws PageFreshFailure carrying askedOnPage. refetchOnMount and retryOnMount are one function: ask only when nothing is in flight and the latest settled ask (data or error) was asked on an earlier page. The query has retry false and staleTime Infinity. retry calls refetch once, and a local askingAgain flag shows loading at once in the retrying component. PageMoveRefresh holds one useState value {lastPathname, page}, updated during render only when the pathname differs, provides page through PageMovesContext and uses no refs. In an effect keyed on page it calls askSharedReadsAgainFor(queryClient, page): cancelQueries, then invalidateQueries, both limited to reads whose latest ask belongs to an earlier page. useRefreshPermissions invalidates with refetchType all.

Note for review (design): to avoid a double ask on a page move, askSharedReadsAgainFor needs to know which page a read's in-flight ask belongs to. The reason is that a component mounting on the new page subscribes, and so asks, in a child effect that runs before the PageMoveRefresh effect. If PageMoveRefresh then invalidated that ask, it would cancel it and ask a second time. The page of each read's latest ask is kept in a module-level WeakMap keyed by the TanStack Query object, in usePageFreshQuery.ts. It is set in the queryFn through context.client. The page counter itself is not in a ref or module variable, as D10 requires, but this per-query map is module state D10 does not name. A plain invalidate does not cancel a first ask that has no data (TanStack joins it instead), which is why cancelQueries runs first.
